wiki_text: Originally proposed as a joint venture with Shell and GDF Suez (later Engie), both foreign partners withdrew from the project in May 2017 after GAIL was unable to guarantee minimum LNG offtake volumes, amid concerns that Indian power plants would not commit to buying imported gas. The project continued for a period under GAIL / Andhra Pradesh Gas Infrastructure Corporation alone before being shelved and cancelled.

topic: Project history / relationship to Krishna Godavari FSRU
wiki_text: The Crown Kakinada LNG Terminal traces to the earlier Krishna Godavari FSRU project (Constellation Energy / Exmar / VGS Group, cancelled around 2021), whose Indian project company was Krishna Godavari LNG Terminal Pvt Ltd ('KGLNG'), holder of the Kakinada operating licence. Crown LNG Holdings acquired 100% of KGLNG in November 2024 for about US$60 million, inheriting the licence, and redesigned the facility from a floating FSRU to a fixed gravity-based storage and regasification unit (GBSRU) of ~7.2 mtpa, with partners cited as Aker Solutions, Siemens and Wartsila. Crown LNG expects a final investment decision in 2026 and first gas in 2029. GEM tracks the cancelled predecessor and the active Crown project as two separate records at the same site, per the convention that a different sponsor and design constitutes a new project.

In early July 2026 IndianOil LNG's proposed expansion of the Ennore terminal -- doubling regasification capacity from 5 to 10 mtpa at an investment of about Rs 3,400 crore (~US$408 million) -- received environmental clearance from India's Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). Environmental clearance is a permitting milestone, not a construction start; as of mid-July 2026 no FID, construction start, or contractor award for the expansion had been reported.
